steps.text: Eight Years Ago
County Oak Grove

steps.name: Witty Noble
steps.text: Your Lordship, more than a paucity are inquiring after you, wondering what our planned next move will be.

steps.name: Witty Noble
steps.text: Our repertoire has been a massive success, all thanks to your backing.

steps.name: Witty Noble
steps.text: The Tarans' own theater, and the Tarans' own history. Two hundred strong came to see the premiere, and my, were they overjoyed.

steps.name: Witty Noble
steps.text: Now, we can pursue joint partnership in a few factories on Baron McAneny's estate, or we can accept this offer of alliance with a number of bankers...

steps.name: Earl of Warwick
steps.text: Leave these topics for after the soirée, Sir Perth. Or have a typist make the arrangements in your stead, and they won't make much mess of it.

steps.name: Earl of Warwick
steps.text: We should talk tonight only of the freshly concluded performance, and of Taran culture. Forget all that Victorian long-windedness and flattery.

steps.name: Earl of Warwick
steps.text: Everyone, all this status and etiquette, this daintiness and diction, this respectable vocabulary we rely on to exchange thoughts, we were taught all of it by the Victorians.

steps.name: Earl of Warwick
steps.text: They're the same as the Victorians' machines, saddling the Tarans' hearts with contemporary ills.

steps.name: Earl of Warwick
steps.text: Time was we only knew our natural highness and valor, and the blood we inherit from King Gaeil would stir without rest at the call of battle...

steps.name: Earl of Warwick
steps.text: But now, we've been trained in the Victorians' guile and vanity, to the point where faced with a true and genuine undertaking, a rally to an ideal, many can only play it as a game in their own interest.

steps.name: Earl of Warwick
steps.text: It is not solely us, either. It goes for the everyday Taran citizen we so often meet in the streets, too.

steps.name: Earl of Warwick
steps.text: Since being contaminated by Victorians' vice, they have become Oripathics, and become rascals, ruffians.

steps.name: Witty Noble
steps.text: Very well said, My Lord—

steps.name: Plain-Dressed Bard
steps.text: —I'm sorry, I accidentally broke my wine glass.

steps.name: Earl of Warwick
steps.text: It seems your glass wished to interject.

steps.name: Plain-Dressed Bard
steps.text: I'd like to ask Your Lordship's opinion on something.

steps.name: Earl of Warwick
steps.text: Pardon my memory, but who might you be...?

steps.name: Plain-Dressed Bard
steps.text: Williams, the bard. Writer of that play that happened tonight. But you don't need to go to the trouble of remembering my name; I can't say I've made much contribution to the literary circles.

steps.name: Earl of Warwick
steps.text: Hardly, Mr. Williams. As I've said, I most detest the Victorians' long-windedness.

steps.name: Earl of Warwick
steps.text: Ask away.

steps.name: Plain-Dressed Bard
steps.text: You've likened the Tarans to a diseased people. How should we heal ourselves in your view, then? How should we save fellow Tarans from the brink?

steps.name: Earl of Warwick
steps.text: I fear no matter how hard we strive, we cannot cure the blight core to us, just as muddied water cannot clean itself.

steps.name: Plain-Dressed Bard
steps.text: So you say it's beyond us to save them, the rascals, the ruffians.

steps.name: Plain-Dressed Bard
steps.text: You don't believe they simply lack for knowledge, education? That the power to help them lives in our pens?

steps.name: Earl of Warwick
steps.text: *sigh* Too fine an intellect is exactly what our enemy is.

steps.name: Earl of Warwick
steps.text: Of course, we write, we rally, we dream of the ideal nation of Tara... We try to rouse the memories of it sleeping in our blood.

steps.name: Earl of Warwick
steps.text: But you and I will have to be the ones to stay behind in these olden days.

steps.name: Earl of Warwick
steps.text: You see, I very much enjoy your works. And yet, we're forced to use the Victorian language.

steps.name: Earl of Warwick
steps.text: 'I lay down now my soldier's honor here, so that in time the soil of Tara need no longer be soaked in carmine blood, and Draco cross no swords with Draco kin.'

steps.name: Earl of Warwick
steps.text: 'Be that unless a day comes, whereupon Red Dragon's flame should lead all those that fell, our fighters from the forge to be reborn.'

steps.name: Plain-Dressed Bard
steps.text: As much as I'm flattered, it's all a simple record of the folk ballads. The most I did was add some metered polish.

steps.name: Earl of Warwick
steps.text: No, I'm just thinking...

steps.name: Earl of Warwick
steps.text: It's no sure thing that Tara will never have another Red Dragon.

steps.name: Earl of Warwick
steps.text: After all, none of us have ever seen a Draco before. How would we tell if whoever passes by us isn't actually a Vouivre?
Village of Redridge, Scáthanna Fields

steps.name: Patrol Member
steps.text: Found them. It was these two mucking about in the streets. Sound of the window breaking must've been their doing.

steps.name: Patrol Member
steps.text: Hey, settle down, you two, or else it's not your wrists the rope goes around next time.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: *spit*!

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Wait—come on, stop being vile now...!

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: I—I'm sorry! I'm sorry, officers! It was our fault!

steps.name: Patrol Captain
steps.text: Is that the wanted lot, the ones rubbing up with Dublinn?

steps.name: Patrol Member
steps.text: One of them's wanted. The other I've never seen.

steps.name: Patrol Captain
steps.text: Heh, I knew these Tarans would all be in on it. Bloody good-for-nothings.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Eek! Please don't do anything, I beg you...

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: This is all we had on us, you searched us and all... Ask us anything you want, we'll explain, we will...

steps.name: Patrol Captain
steps.text: Shut up. What are your pals up to, eh? Where'd they go? Are they off gossiping info to Dublinn?

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: I—I don't know, honestly, I don't...

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: We don't even have any pals! We've never met anyone from Dublinn before!

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: And you just want some people to beat to death, give yourself something to report to your noble brass!

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: *spit*! You... you bloody Victorian scumbags!

steps.name: Patrol Captain
steps.text: Keeping mum, are you?

steps.name: Patrol Captain
steps.text: Take them inside. Don't let these ballsacks make their racket on the street. They'll wake the rest of us up.

steps.name: Patrol Captain
steps.text: Question the one with the bag first. If he's honest, he can suffer a little less.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: I—I'm honest, I'm an honest person, I swear, I don't know a thing...

steps.name: Patrol Member
steps.text: Hold on, Captain.

steps.name: Patrol Member
steps.text: I think there's more nearby.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Uh, the—there's...

steps.name: Patrol Member
steps.text: What's bag boy shouting about?

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Fire!

steps.name: Patrol Member
steps.text: Shut UP! Don't try and cover for your friends—

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: —No, but there's a fire off behind you!

steps.name: Patrol Member
steps.text: It's the warehouse!

steps.name: Patrol Captain
steps.text: Bloody Nora! I want the word out to Team 1! Prioritize firefighting!

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Er, did they dump us and go?

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Fionn, come on, undo my ropes here!

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: H—How? I'm tied up too...

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Who are you?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Let's go, quick.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: *huff* I'm sorry you had to run with us. You've got nothing to do with this...

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: ...It's fine, we shook them off.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Hey, Fionn, the radio?

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Right here. Should still be usable, just a little quiet.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Quiet's good. Keeps us from being found.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: *sigh* You listen for any word, I'll go wash my face at the pond. Try and calm down.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Excuse me, Vouivre. You can go if it's dangerous to you. I'll point you on your way.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: No need... I can wait here, and keep watch for you.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: ...Alright, thank you. You're a good one, truly.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: (Deep breath)

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: No nerves, Fionn, no nerves. Out of sight, out of mind.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: You didn't touch blood. It is not blood. It's just marshy mud. Wash it off and it'll be fine...

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: ...Hfff.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: *sigh*.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Bollocks... hey! You swear this stupid thing still works?

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Shush, god's sakes! Those army lot can't be far away!

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Give it a few more knocks, then crank it!

steps.name: Voice on the Airwaves
steps.text: ...approximately 9:30 PM...

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: There.

steps.name: Voice on the Airwaves
steps.text: A case of arson in a settlement close to the County Trent... methods resemble those of the Dublinn insurrectionists...

steps.name: Voice on the Airwaves
steps.text: ...the three suspected are still on the run...

steps.name: Voice on the Airwaves
steps.text: Should... clues on Dublinn elements not report them to the authorities... considered equally guilty as these rebels...

steps.name: Voice on the Airwaves
steps.text: ...warn you once again... the lights-out bell, you are not to go outside. All areas apart from mines and factories are forbidden from lighting any lamps whatsoever...

steps.name: Voice on the Airwaves
steps.text: Put a stop... all activities related to these insurgents...

steps.name: Voice on the Airwaves
steps.text: (White noise)

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Diabhal. They really broadcast nothing else past 9 PM.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: What are these bloody rules, in ainm Dé?

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Sorry. That's a foul tongue for Taran. Could you understand that?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Yes... but that's fine.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: No, still, I'm sorry. For dragging an outsider like you into this.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: It's okay... Tarans are the same, no matter where they are.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I once visited the Scáthanna Fields, myself. But they didn't have rules about lights-out back then.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Ó, I'm guessing you're from a nomadic city, then?

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Bell-ringing as law has been around for years. Used to just be out on the barrens, to mind whoever tried sneaking into whatever count or viscount's hunting grounds at dead midnight.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Bell rings, we snuff the lamps, and fires go out too. If someone in the barrens lights a fire to herd beasts at this hour, you can see it clear as day from miles and miles away.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: But muck-ups like today only happened once the new rules got stricter. Those night patrol tossers see anyone in the street, they snatch 'em.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: There, Fionn. Calmed down?

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Suppose so...

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: ...Er, where's our medicine? Are we all out?

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Take a guess?

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: ...*sigh*. Shame about my fountain pen. Can't even note my own debts now.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Stealing is what we're doing. Don't think you have to make up for it with what you've got.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: How many days have we been outdoors now?

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: If it's not midnight yet, then it's day 12 for us.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Alright. Twelve days, and we've barely gotten far. I keep thinking if only it'd clear up, I might see chimney smoke or something from a village.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: We've just been hounded by the army, chased around in circles here...

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Be honest, do you really think we can make it out?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: ...What happened with you two?

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: We had a little confrontation with the patrol. They sent a warrant out for us.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Fionn!

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Let me talk, Fergal. I can feel, this lady's a good person.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: When the patrol came here to make arrests, they summoned everyone who had a record. And then they started with the beatings, so we fought back...

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: You didn't, Fionn. Don't give yourself credit.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Ugh, okay.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: We hadn't done all that bad, really, truth told. One family ran after they couldn't pay tax dues, so the patrol was dragging all their relatives in by the scruff for questioning. Fergal was brewing a little moonshine just for himself, and I'd missed some formalities while selling stuff.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: *sigh* We'd always owned up properly too, whatever it was. It all got too much that day.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: It wasn't just us two who scarpered once the patrol started beating. It's ten or so of us, all summoned that day by the army. We all ran at once.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: But if the army wants someone, there's no escaping it. That lot won't change their tune just because someone's word says they're innocent.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: You ended up killing someone?

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Yeah, we did two of 'em in. Got one straight off with a hoe while they weren't on guard, the other we laid low in the whole scuffle.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Shame we let the third one do a runner, or else the army'd never know about what we did.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Hey! We wouldn't be in such a miserable spot if we'd had one night more of a head start.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: ...Fergal, you think we could... give ourselves up to them? I could do it alone, even. Just can't stand these days on the run anymore.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: We didn't even nab the medicine. Oran's cut's just festering away, and he's... I can't take it, I can't.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: You drop the bloody idea. You think they'd make it easy on you?

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Bloody wouldn't. They'd torture you first, crush your spirits.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Two minutes with someone like you, and they'd get everything about us pouring out.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Look. We've got no meds. Torture by sickness, that's torture all the same, yeah?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Are you—short of medicine?

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Haha... we were sent out to rustle up some more, I'll say. They're waiting for us, a decent ways back somewhere.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: We were here planning to buy it, honest.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: But we knew in our heads, all the shops'd shut the moment lights-out sounded. We'd never make it in time beforehand.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: So we got a rough idea of when the patrol changes shifts, er, and we smashed through a shop window... I thought they wouldn't notice around about then.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: ...God.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: ...You? Guessing you're from the city. What got you out in this desolate a place?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: ...I'm searching for some things.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Do you—know about 'Dublinn'?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Yes, I understand.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I have some—antihemorrhagics and bandages on me, actually.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Mr. Fionn, I saw you were hurt... we should sort that out.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Oh, you noticed? It's nothing big, really...

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: But—if you're willing to share a bit of medicals with me, that'd be fair play.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Our mates are hurt far worse. I'd bring 'em to them, if that's okay.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Er, they got bit by gloompincers.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: In that case, I can go with you...

steps.name: Patrol Member
steps.text: That way! We have footprints in the mud, leading that way!

steps.name: Patrol Member
steps.text: It's the Tara rabble behind the arson! They're around here, no doubt!

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: —Q-Quick, hide!

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: It's... it's a whole unit, half a dozen people, they're shining their torches this way!

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Quick, bend down, come this way! It's solid ground here!

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: It's alright... those soldiers won't dare to move too fast through the marsh.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: —Shh.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: (Fionn, I can hear your teeth chattering!)
A torch flashes over them.
Reed grips her spear tight, the metal warming, hotter and hotter.

steps.name: Dublinn Soldier?
steps.text: Well, that's shite! How come you lot get torches?! Pisses me off just seeing you!

steps.name: Patrol Member
steps.text: Dublinn?!

steps.name: Patrol Member
steps.text: Get her! She's got info, no doubt!

steps.name: Dublinn Soldier?
steps.text: Get me? You're codding me!

steps.name: Patrol Member
steps.text: Peuch! What're you slinging mud for?

steps.name: Patrol Member
steps.text: Ugh—

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Come on, Fionn, we've got to help her! Don't be a coward!

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Alright, alright, okay...

steps.name: Patrol Member
steps.text: Urgh—!

steps.name: Dublinn Soldier?
steps.text: Hah, couple of fresh boys don't take much to sort out.

steps.name: Dublinn Soldier?
steps.text: Hey, Fionn, Fergal! You made a right hames here, didn't you? Would've kicked the bucket if I didn't come looking, no?

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: No, yeah. Saved our skins. All thanks to you.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: I told you, see, all this smashing and looting business might be beyond me...

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Wait, what are you doing, Selmon? It's enough to knock them out. You're going to kill them all?

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Aren't we going to be more guilty for that?!

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Same difference! It doesn't matter how guilty if they're after a Taran—you get taken in, you're not coming out alive.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: *sigh* It makes a difference in my head.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Coward. You watch, I'm gonna do all these Victorian bastards right and—

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Stop. Don't do that.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: And who do you think you are?

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Hah, what's the staring for? Gonna be a tattletale? Just you try.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Tattle? No, you're not even part of Dublinn. Why are you... dressed like that?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Why are you copying the Spectre Force's methods?

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: —And on what basis do you claim that? You some Dublinn know-it-all?

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Er, calm, now, Selmon.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: She's just a doctor. She was doing a runner with us just now...

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: ...I think she's a good soul. I told her all about us.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Right, um, doctor... what you said about taking a look at our wounded, is that still valid?

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Selmon, honest, you need to cool it... We mucked it all up. We didn't get the medicine. This kind doctor says she can help us, so that's all we can rely on now.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Tch, leave me out of this. Seems this doctor here recognizes my clothes.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: ...I'm sorry, I'm not a doctor.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: But I still want—to try and help you.
